evidence.quote: [page/0/Text/4] individual cognitive behavior therapy, systemic behavior family therapy (SBFT), or individual nondirective supportive therapy (NST)
[/page/1/Text/12] Cognitive behavior therapy (CBT)

[/page/1/Text/15] During the second phase, which was adapted from the problemsolving model developed by Robin and Foster,37 the family members focus on communication and problemsolving skills and the alteration of family interactional patterns. Systemic behavior family therapy provides extensive socialization to the treatment model and education about depression, parenting and developmental issues and emphasizes skill building and positive practice in sessions and at home.

[/page/2/Text/0] Adherence to CBT was monitored by the 11-item Cognitive Therapy Rating Scale, 38 to SBFT by a modification of the 12-item Family Therapist Rating Scale, 39 and to NST by 8 items adapted from the Vanderbilt Psychotherapy Process Scale.

[/page/3/Text/13] To examine the efficacy of different psychotherapeutic approaches, we compared individual CBT and family treatment approaches to adolescent depression with nondirective supportive therapy (NST) as a third cell to control for the nonspecific effects of psychotherapy.

Adherence to CBT was monitored by the 11-item Cognitive Therapy Rating Scale, 38 to SBFT by a modification of the 12-item Family Therapist Rating Scale, 39 and to NST by 8 items adapted from the Vanderbilt Psychotherapy Process Scale. 40 All 3 instruments had Likert responses from 0 (poor) to 6 (excellent), with increasing scores for more adherence and a 4 on each item as the lowest acceptable score.
